stem:
$\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{I}_2\text{(g)}$ react to form $\text{HI(g)}$ in a reversible reaction, as shown in equation 1.

equation 1 $$\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI(g)}$$

In three separate experiments, a student combines different amounts of two or more of the gases from equation 1. In each experiment, the gases are left to reach equilibrium at a given temperature.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
In experiment 1, $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{I}_2\text{(g)}$ are combined.

Water is then added to the equilibrium mixture to produce $1.00\text{ dm}^3$ of solution **A**.

The amount of $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ present in $1.00\text{ dm}^3$ of solution **A** is found by titration with $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3\text{(aq)}$.

Exactly $32.90\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.200\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ reacts with all of the $\text{I}_2$ in a $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ sample of solution **A**.

$$\text{I}_2\text{(aq)} + 2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{I}^-\text{(aq)} + \text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}\text{(aq)}$$
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in mol, of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$ that reacts in the titration.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Use your answer to **(a)(i)** to calculate the amount, in mol, of $\text{I}_2$ present in $1.00\text{ dm}^3$ of solution **A**.

(If you were unable to obtain an answer in **(a)(i)**, then use $9.42 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$. This is **not** the correct answer.)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
In experiment 2, $0.100\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$, $0.200\text{ mol}$ of $\text{I}_2\text{(g)}$ and $0.300\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HI(g)}$ are combined.

At equilibrium $0.154\text{ mol}$ of $\text{I}_2$ is present.

Calculate the amounts, in mol, of $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{HI}$ in the equilibrium mixture produced in experiment 2.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
In experiment 3, $0.0772\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2$ and $0.0986\text{ mol}$ of $\text{I}_2$ are present in an equilibrium mixture at $298\text{ K}$.

$$\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI(g)} \hspace{2cm} K_\text{c} = 7.94 \times 10^2$$

Use the equilibrium constant, $K_\text{c}$, to calculate the amount, in mol, of $\text{HI}$ present in the equilibrium mixture in experiment 3.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
The value of $K_\text{c}$ for the dissociation of $\text{HCl}$ at $298\text{ K}$ is $5.50 \times 10^{-34}$.

$$2\text{HCl(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \hspace{2cm} K_\text{c} = 5.50 \times 10^{-34}$$

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Describe and explain the relative thermal stabilities of the hydrogen halides $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HI}$.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Use the data given in **(c)** and **(d)** to suggest a value for the equilibrium constant for the **dissociation** of $\text{HBr(g)}$ at $298\text{ K}$.
